---
title: "Python for Bioinformatics"
subtitle: "From first principles to writing your own tools"
---

A hands-on course that takes you from basic Python to building packaged, command-line, version-controlled bioinformatics tools and reproducible pipelines. Every example uses a real pathogen-genomics theme.

## The four parts

| Part | Focus |
|---|---|
| [I — Foundations](PartI-theory.qmd) | setup, syntax, strings & sequences, control flow, data structures, functions |
| [II — Real Programming](PartII-theory.qmd) | files (FASTA/FASTQ/CSV), errors/debugging/testing, object-oriented programming |
| [III — The Ecosystem](PartIII-theory.qmd) | NumPy, pandas, matplotlib/seaborn, Biopython |
| [IV — Your Own Tools & Pipelines](PartIV-theory.qmd) | environments & git, CLI tools, packaging, subprocess, pysam/VCF/Entrez, Snakemake |

Each part has **theory** and a **code** page with the exercises and solutions (downloadable Jupyter notebooks).

## Setup

```bash
# create the course environment (conda recommended)
conda create -n biopy python=3.11
conda activate biopy
conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda numpy pandas matplotlib seaborn biopython jupyterlab
# Part IV adds:
conda install -c bioconda pysam snakemake
pip install cyvcf2
```

Example data is in [downloads/python/data](../downloads/python/data).
